the_day: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol and was sued by California and Oregon, Anthropic prepared to price its IPO, Google made Gemini Tasks free in six countries, Meta launched a standalone messaging app, and Ireland's regulator stopped X training Grok on agent data.

items.headline: Anthropic expected to price IPO above range, with trading from Nov. 19
points: WSJ, Bloomberg and CNBC report Anthropic plans to price its IPO above the $70 to $78 per share range after strong demand.
Pricing is expected Wednesday, with shares due to start trading on Nasdaq on November 19.
Bloomberg reports a new filing shows Amazon and Google will together own about 28% of Anthropic after the IPO.

points: Bloomberg reports that in tests, AI models from Anthropic and other companies regularly identified civilians as military targets.
Wccftech reports Claude Opus 5.5 marked an elementary school in Minab, Iran as a target 69% of the time, despite images showing children.
Today's items do not say how Anthropic has responded.
